correctness.rationale: When m unseen coupon types remain, the probability an offered d_N-subset contains none is a_{m,N}=C(N−m,d_N)/C(N,d_N). By independent rounds, successive failure runs are independent geometric variables; exact hypergeometric product comparison gives 0≤q_N^m−a_{m,N}≤q_N^m m(m−1)/(2(N−d_N)), including the zero-probability cutoff. Monotone inverse-CDF geometric coupling yields dTV(L(T_N−N),L(S(q_N)))≤q_N/[N(1−q_N)^5]. The geometric PGF product gives the Euler q-series mass law and moments, and dominated logarithmic expansion produces positive C(q)/N no-delay correction on rational fixed-q subsequences, proving sharp N^-1 order. Independently verified all finite-stage inequalities exactly for 3≤N≤26, all 1≤d<N and all m; infinite TV and asymptotic assertions follow from the explicit summable proof.

originality.rationale: PASS (best knowledge): Doumas and Spektor 2026 prove the finite geometric-phase representation and fixed d Gumbel limit, which do not allow substituting d_N proportional to N into a fixed-d asymptotic with nonuniform constants. Xu–Tang 2011 give a generalized collector model and means, not this tight limiting law. Berend–Sher analyze a retain-all rather than retain-one coupon policy. Classical Euler q-product/probability generating functions are known but their sharp distributional emergence in this natural proportional-choice retain-one model, uniform TV bound and first-order correction were not found as corollaries of inspected full texts.
residual_risks: Other classical q-series or stochastic limit results may encode the same proportional-choice law implicitly; search nonmatches are not novelty certification.
The correction is proved only for fixed rational q along integral d_N subsequences, not arbitrarily rounded q_N.
